title: Tottenham Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency medical centers, urgent care, and Lea Valley flood zones for Tottenham.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, always call 999 or 112 immediately.

1. Nearest 24-Hour A&E Hospitals:
- North Middlesex University Hospital (24-Hour A&E): Sterling Way, London N18 1QX. From White Hart Lane station: ~20 min walk north along High Road and east along Bull Lane/Sterling Way (approx. 1 mile), or take bus 149, 259, 279, or 349 north to the hospital entrance.
- Whittington Hospital (24-Hour A&E): Magdala Avenue, Archway, London N19 5NF. From Seven Sisters station: take bus 41 west via Tottenham Green and Crouch End towards Archway.

2. NHS Urgent Treatment Centres:
- North Middlesex Hospital Urgent Treatment Centre: Sterling Way, London N18 1QX. Open 24/7 on-site alongside the main emergency department.
- Broadwater Farm Health Centre (Walk-in services): 2a Willan Road, London N17 6BF. From Bruce Grove station: ~15 min walk west along The Avenue and Mount Pleasant Road.

3. Local Hazard Notes:
- River Lea & Moselle Brook: The River Lea corridor, Tottenham Marshes, and flood basins east of Tottenham Hale are vulnerable to high water levels and marshland runoff during heavy prolonged rain.
- Low-lying Underpasses: The Ferry Lane and Hale Village transit underpasses can flood rapidly.

4. Essential Supplies:
Supermarkets and dispensing chemists on Tottenham High Road, West Green Road, and Tottenham Hale Retail Park stock fresh water, first-aid items, and staple medications.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible (verify locally).
